title: Artifact frontmatter
description: The machine header carried by every artifact of the authoring standard (IDE-78). Prose cannot be validated; this header can. Which fields are required depends on 'type'.

type.description: Which artifact this is. It selects both the required header fields and the MD043 heading list used to lint the body.

status.description: Approval state of an ADR. Only an ADR has one: a card's state lives on the board, not in its text.

route.description: How many gates this work passes: feature — three, small-feature — two (no ADR is written), bug — one. Process metadata, not a plan, which is why it lives in the header and not in a section.

standard.description: Version of the authoring standard this artifact was written against. A new version never invalidates older artifacts retroactively; touching an artifact pulls it up to the current version.

cid.description: Correlation identifier tying a feature to its ADR and to the issues produced from it, across trackers. The value format is owned by the Feature Discovery package contract (IDE-68); here it is only required to be present and non-empty.

parent.description: Identifier of the issue this artifact hangs from — the feature, for an ADR, a PBI and its agent attachment. The IDE prefix is this project's team key.

scope.description: Which level a decision was taken at. Absent means the feature level, which is every ADR the architect writes. 'project' marks the one ADR that describes the whole system: it hangs from the epic rather than a feature, and feature-level ADRs link to it and record only their delta.

discovery.description: Whether this feature has been thought through. 'required' means it was sliced out of a project architecture without enough behind it and cannot move until Feature Discovery has run on it; 'done' means Discovery lifted the block. Absent means the feature never came from a slice. The block lives here rather than in a board status because Linear has no API for creating statuses, and a tenth status would be a manual step on every foreign board.

stage.description: Which stage of the project this feature belongs to. Stages come out of the traced end-to-end scenarios, the first being the walking skeleton. Cards exist only for the open stage; later stages live as one line in the project ADR until their turn.

then.$comment: No `route` and no `parent`. Routes count the gates one piece of work passes and a whole project is not one piece of work; `parent` is an issue identifier, and the epic that carries this ADR is a project on Linear, which has none.

allOf.$comment: `scope` belongs to an ADR alone: nothing else is decided at two levels.
`discovery` and `stage` describe a feature that came out of a slice.
